7) The growth of sharks can be modeled using [von Bertalanffy curves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Von_Bertalanffy_function). Scalloped hammerhead sharks in the Atlantic were found to have growth curves that follow the graph below.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code  code-fold="true" code-summary="Show the code"}
vb<-function(a,l,k,t0){
  l*(1-exp(-k*(a-t0)))
}

x=seq(0,30)

length=vb(x,214.8,.13,-1.62)

p1<-ggplot()+
  geom_point(aes(x=x,y=length),color="black",size=3)+
  geom_line(aes(x=x,y=length),color="black",size=2)+
  theme_bw()+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(35,215,5))+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(0,32,by=2))+
  labs(x="Age (years)",y="Length (cm)")

p1
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](day3-problem-set_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


  a) What is the average slope from ages 0 to 8? From 20 to 30?
    
  b) What are the units of the average slopes and why would they change for a shark as they get older?
    
  c) How would you find the instantaneous slope for a shark at age 12? What is the closest approximation you can make with this data and graph?

## Exercise 2

A stream's water temperature increases as you move downstream from a shaded headwater spring. At a monitoring station 2 km downstream, the water temperature is 14°C. At a station 5 km downstream, the temperature is 20°C. Assume temperature increases linearly with distance downstream.

(a) Find the equation for water temperature $T$ (°C) as a function of distance downstream $x$ (km).
(b) Create a plot showing the line. Clearly label the axes, including units, and add a title.
(c) What is the $y$-intercept of this line, and what does it mean in the context of the stream? Answer in a full sentence.
